meaning: The external form of the problem of evil needs the premise that there is evil, asserted as true (ST I q.2 a.3 obj. 1, STMT-EVIL-PREMISE-IS-TRUE). From O'Connor's emotivism (moral statements have no truth value), his own gloss (what has no truth value is not true), his classification of badness ascriptions as moral, and the bridge that the evil premise says something is bad (q.2 a.3 obj. 1), it follows that the evil premise is not true. The external premise therefore contradicts his own commitments. Each bridge is its own sourced statement. Because the theorem uses only truth, it also covers 'objectively true'. It does not touch the internal form, which O'Connor can run on the theist's own standard (see POE-CATHOLIC-CONSISTENT-WITH-EVIL). The Comparator config also verifies `emotivismConsistentWithBackground`: emotivism is consistent with the shared background, so what it contradicts is the evil premise, not the background. Proof shape, stated plainly: three steps (the evil premise is moral because it says something is bad; emotivism then denies it a truth value; the gloss then denies it truth). No premise already states the conclusion. The content lies in the four separately sourced premises.
